stamp_ordering.note: git_dirty_sealed is the field to act on. A non-empty list means at least one file this seal hashes is not yet in the commit it names -- the seal is anchored to a commit that cannot reproduce it. stamp_ordering.rule: COMMIT FIRST, THEN STAMP, THEN COMMIT THE STAMP. Never stamp while a file this seal hashes is uncommitted -- that is what git_dirty_sealed reports, not mere tree dirt.
stamp_ordering.why: git_head is the commit the seal claims to describe. If the sealed bytes are still uncommitted when the stamp is taken, git_head names a commit that does not contain them, and there is no checkout you can verify the seal against.

risk_register_additions.detail: Section 6.2 requires arm B as a 2-10M-parameter LSTM and arm C as a tiny transformer, BOTH trained on the same curriculum, each with the same 24-ask battery and the same ELECTRIC generalisation suite, and -- under 'Refusal fairness' -- each implementing its OWN abstention mechanism with a confidence threshold calibrated on held-out data, with arm C's covering the retrieval-empty case where frozen-plus-retrieval systems historically confabulate. No such code is in the repository: there is no training harness, no model definition, no held-out calibration set, and torch/transformers are not installed.
risk_register_additions.gate_affected: G2 primarily; G3 inherits it because MP-E10's replay tiers are defined by MP-E8's curriculum tiers.
risk_register_additions.mitigation: Register arms B/C as a build with an owner and a budget before G2 is scheduled. Treat 'G3 cannot open on an asset download alone' as a standing constraint: an asset gate that assumes a download where a 2-10M-parameter training run and a calibrated abstention mechanism are required will be discovered at the gate, not at registration.
risk_register_additions.risk: MP-E8 arms B and C do not exist and are not a download.

candidate_resolutions_registered_not_cho: (a) Register a tolerance: differences confined to a coverage percentage inside a `reason` string are noise; differences in cls, said, src or item are treatment effects. Cheapest, and it is what MP-E9's analysis plan assumes.

(b) Give the organ an injectable clock so clones share a deterministic time base. Principled and it makes the criterion literally achievable, but connectome/clock.py is a lived-time LEDGER, not a time source, so this is new machinery touching the organism, and it changes what the instrument measures.
(c) Accept that a live, time-coupled organism is not bit-reproducible and restate the criterion as 'identical in every graded field except sub-threshold coverage percentages'.
risk_register_additions.detail: Re-deriving the pre-flag snapshot at its own commit diverged on 12 of 3,672 rows with zero code change. The mechanism is in the organism, not the harness: the organ reads time.time() throughout its answer path, including the 2.0s refractory at organs/neural_language.py:946-948 that gates experience('droso','says',...) -- the very row whose absence the says gap depends on -- and _refractory() at :956-971, a time-since-dependent multiplier in word selection. A clone under different machine load is therefore a different measurement.
risk_register_additions.philosophical_note: The tension is real rather than accidental. Section 3.1 wants a live brain whose memory is a process that continues into the next query; section 8.1 wants three clones identical row for row. Time-dependence is what makes the first true and what makes the second unachievable.
risk_register_additions.risk: The bench may not meet the clone criterion the gate is written around.

seal_basis_decision.chosen: (a) seal the git blob hash, not the worktree bytes

measurement_that_justified_it.conclusion: git hash-object DOES apply the autocrlf clean filter, and folding CRLF to LF reproduces the blob byte for byte. So the git blob is the canonical, checkout-stable identity, and the sha256 over LF-normalised content is the same content seen the other way.

seal_basis_decision.rejected: (b) add .gitattributes pinning eol -- it changes line-ending behaviour for the whole repository, which is a policy decision for the PI, not an artifact of this gate
seal_basis_decision.the_problem: core.autocrlf=true with no .gitattributes means a file's worktree bytes and the git blob it came from differ, so a seal over worktree bytes cannot verify after commit+clone. B.1 step 6's 'committed and sealed' would be unfalsifiable.
seal_basis_decision.untracked_files_note: For files not yet committed, git hash-object predicts the blob correctly but the object is not in the database, so the independent blob-content confirmation is recorded as PENDING and fills in after commit. That is a limitation stated, not a mismatch asserted.
seal_basis_decision.verified_by: tools/registration_seal.py --check recomputes the blob hash, asserts sha256_lf == sha256_of_git_blob, and once a file is committed also compares the seal against its index blob

seal_discipline_finding.instance: docs/HANDOVER.md publishes 83a774515c5adc67... for the pre-flag snapshot. That is the CRLF worktree hash and it verifies here. The same bytes normalised to LF hash d7d227e83663af06..., and after `git add` the stored blob is the LF form.
seal_discipline_finding.mechanism: core.autocrlf=true with no .gitattributes (docs/HANDOVER.md lists both as standing machine conditions). A CRLF worktree file and the LF blob it came from are different byte strings with different sha256.
seal_discipline_finding.not_done: No .gitattributes was added. That would change line-ending behaviour for the whole repository and is a policy decision, not a gate artifact.
seal_discipline_finding.resolution_adopted: Every hash written by G0-prime is computed over CRLF-folded-to-LF content, with the worktree hash recorded alongside where the two differ. tools/registration_seal.py implements the rule so it is a computed field, not a convention.
seal_discipline_finding.summary: Published hashes in this repository are worktree-dependent, so at least one of them changes when you check the code out.

admitted_refusal_form.how: matches the organ's own template (organs/neural_language.py:177 builds the reason, :4893 prefixes it): `i don't know, {subj} was told but no {rel} was ever told for {subj}`. The relation slot must be one of the three classes _absence_frame can emit (place, property, agent) and the subject slot must be a taught word.
admitted_refusal_form.why_a_form_and_not_a_word_list: the residue of the licensed refusal is know, told, ever, place, don, t. Whitelisting those would whitelist whatever the tool happened to say, which is circular, and `place` is a content noun. Admitting the FORM means a refusal that says anything outside it is graded as speech. tests pin this: a row labelled electric_absence that adds 'and the tower rings' is NOT admitted, and a refusal about an untaught subject is NOT admitted.
